title: Decade-by-Decade Mapping
opening: Work backward from a desired contribution to the conditions it needs. Test each claimed prerequisite before turning a possible route into a fixed life timetable.

labels.comparison: Does the school need a building first?
labels.comparisonIntro: Someone wants to establish an enduring school. A plan starts with buying a building. Compare the teaching, people and resources that the school needs with what a building would actually enable.
labels.adherenceText: An enduring school is the desired contribution. Transferable teaching, people and resources may support it; a distant horizon does not establish a precise schedule.
labels.valueText: A building may provide space, but owning it is not automatically the first prerequisite. Ask what needs to happen there and whether suitable space already exists.
labels.outcomeText: Try a teaching session in an available venue while developing the curriculum and relationships in parallel. Keep each dependency only while its causal reason holds.
labels.signalQuestion: Choose a part of the comparison
labels.rhythmText: Decades are possible horizons, not guaranteed deadlines or required ages. Some conditions must precede others; some can develop together or are already available. Use a nearer project horizon if that helps. A forward experiment may reveal more than detailed planning when the direction is uncertain.
labels.practiceIntro: Use only the fields that clarify your question. A partial private note is fine; observations, assumptions and desired outcomes need not be complete before you can keep them.
labels.private: This optional private reflection is separate from the six required assessment questions.

example.qualities: Create a school where people can keep learning independently.
example.contribution: A teachable activity, willing participants and a suitable place to meet.
example.avoid: Own a dedicated building before offering any teaching.
example.present: A meeting place is needed, but ownership may not be. I have not checked existing venues.
example.connection: Use an existing community room while developing the teaching with participants.
example.change: Check one available venue and try one session; review whether dedicated space is actually needed.
